uncertain.note: the glyph after 'me' is read as the italic marker ſ (it is slanted and has a descender, unlike the roman ſ of 'meſme' beside it); p003 ends 'à la fem-', so the word completed here is 'femme'. If the glyph were instead a roman long s the word would be 'mes' (= 'femmes') and the page would have no ſ marker for margin note 1. Reading chosen on the marker alphabet (p003's last foot note is keyed r, this page's first margin note is keyed ſ).
the first one or two letters are lost under an ink blot; 'res.' (continuing 'pube-' from the previous line) is the best reading, only '…rs.' is actually legible
a very faint mark follows 'leg' (a period or an end-of-line hyphen), not transcribed; a small dash is also printed immediately before the key letter y of the next note, apparently stray type
the final numeral is 'iij' on my reading (three strokes, the last a j with the ij dots); it could be 'ij'
